main_text.p: oleribus in cibo vti conueniat infrà Deo inspirante, dicemus.
Febri in qua exteriora frigent, & interiora calent, & econtra, quis cōueniat uictus.
main_text.head: CAPVT XXV.

p.i: FEBRIS in qua exteriora frigent et calent interiora, à bili putrescente ortū habet. In qua febrili calore phlegmata crassa in exterioribus existentia dissoluente, accidit partes externas infrigidari, æstuantibus internis. Subtili ideo indigent victu, quia febrilis calor multoties in seipsum reduplicatur transpiratione prohibita. Quapropter periculo non vacat hæc febris, sicut cum à revocatione natiui calidi exteriora frigent. Cibus ijs conuenit refrigerans: cui misceantur ea quæ aperire & valenter incidere valeat.
Post calidam & asperam totius corporis fricationem, hunc febricitanti cibum ministrato: Ptisanam cum radicibus apij & petroselini, et lenticula aquæ parato, coquitoq

page.notes: Drop-cap F in "FEBRIS" is a large woodcut initial, joined to the word. Text on the facing page shows through faintly and is not transcribed. The line "coquitoq" ends with a printed abbreviation mark (ꝗ-type) that is uncertain.
